newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS Bank sees no pain from Thai Danu bank.
newsitem.headline: DBS Bank sees no pain from Thai Danu bank.

text.p: The Development Bank of Singapore Ltd (DBS) said on Thursday it did not expect problems with any of its Thai investments as a result of the current shake-out in Thailand's banking sector.

DBS Bank President Ng Kee Choe told reporters after the release of the group's 1996 financial results that recent media reports of possible "pain" for DBS in connection with its stake in Thai Danu Bank were incorrect.
"Thai Danu Bank is a very solid bank," he said. "The profits are consistently up. The cost of our investment is much lower than even the (bank's) current market value."
The Thai government has admitted its banks and finance companies are grappling with a huge liquidity problem caused by bad debts, many linked to the besieged property sector.
The Thai central bank announced a raft of measures on Monday to improve provisions for bad loans in the sector.

Thai Danu announced at the weekend it would merge with Thailand's largest finance company Finance One Plc, which has been the subject of various rumours in recent days concerning a possible run on its deposits.
